import numpy as np

def dynamics(t, x, u):
    i_L = x[0]  # inductor current (A)
    V_out = x[1]  # output voltage (V)
    D = u[0]  # duty cycle (0 to 1)
    ESR_L = 0.1  # inductor ESR (ohm)
    ESR_C = 0.05  # capacitor ESR (ohm)
    V_in = 12.0  # input voltage (V)
    V_target = 48.0  # target output voltage (V)
    f_s = 100000.0  # switching frequency (Hz)
    L = 0.01  # inductance (H) - assumed value

    # Inductor voltage equation
    V_L = V_in - V_out + i_L * ESR_L
    # Output voltage dynamics
    dV_out_dt = (D * V_in - V_out / ESR_C) / (1 / f_s)
    # Inductor current dynamics
    di_L_dt = V_L / L  # L is the inductance (H)

    dx = np.array([di_L_dt, dV_out_dt])
    return dx
